data.name: Mee Kati
data.description: Thin rice noodles glisten with creamy coconut sauce, tangy tamarind and savory fermented soybean paste. Tender tofu, fragrant shallots and golden omelet ribbons make a comforting Thai breakfast.

not_suitable_for: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease unless the fermented soybean paste is certified gluten-free

refrigerator.notes: Transfer leftovers into shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when the ambient temperature exceeds 32°C (90°F). Store at 4°C (40°F) or below, with omelet strips separate if practical.

freezer.notes: Freezing is not recommended because the fine noodles soften and the coconut sauce may separate.

storage.reheating: Reheat gently in a covered skillet, stirring carefully, until the noodles, tofu and omelet reach 74°C (165°F) throughout. Add a little water if needed to loosen the sauce.

items.name: thin rice vermicelli
items.notes: Use fine Thai sen mee with a warm-water soaking time of approximately 10 minutes; thicker rice noodles require a different schedule.

items.name: water
items.notes: For submerging and softening the noodles; drain and discard after soaking.

items.name: coconut milk
items.notes: Stir the coconut cream and liquid together before weighing.

items.name: firm tofu
items.notes: Edible weight after draining; plain firm or firm yellow tofu works well.

items.name: thai fermented soybean paste
items.notes: Use tao jiew, also sold as yellow soybean sauce. Stir before weighing and choose a product without fish or shellfish ingredients. Some brands contain wheat.

items.name: tamarind puree
items.notes: Use spoonable, single-strength puree, not a highly concentrated tamarind extract.

items.name: water
items.notes: Added to the sauce and served with the noodles.

items.name: canola oil
items.notes: For sauteing the shallot and garlic.

items.name: egg
items.notes: Weight without shells; approximately 2 large eggs.

items.name: canola oil
items.notes: For coating the skillet when cooking the omelet.

items.name: garlic chives
items.notes: Edible weight after removing damaged ends.

instructions.text: Soak the rice vermicelli in the large heatproof bowl with the 1500 g soaking water at approximately 50°C (122°F) for 10 minutes, or according to the package, until flexible but still slightly firm. Complete the vegetable preparation while they soak.

doneness_cues.tactile: Strands bend easily but retain a slightly firm center.

instructions.text: Cut the shallot into thin slices, the garlic into fine pieces, the tofu into 1 cm cubes and the garlic chives into 3 cm lengths using the knife and cutting board.
Drain the softened noodles thoroughly in the colander, discarding the soaking water.
Beat the eggs in the small bowl with the fork until the whites and yolks are evenly combined.

Cook the beaten eggs in the large nonstick skillet with the 5 g omelet oil over medium-low heat, tilting the skillet to form a thin layer. Use the spatula to turn the omelet once its underside sets, and continue until both sides are set and its center reaches 71°C (160°F), about 3 minutes.

doneness_cues.visual: The omelet is lightly golden with no wet or translucent egg.

instructions.text: Rest the cooked omelet on the plate while you prepare the sauce.
Saute the shallot and garlic in the same skillet with the remaining 5 g oil over medium-low heat for 2 minutes, stirring with the spatula until fragrant and softened.

doneness_cues.visual: The shallot becomes translucent and the garlic remains pale.

instructions.text: Stir the coconut milk, fermented soybean paste, tamarind puree, palm sugar, tofu and 80 g sauce water into the aromatics until evenly combined.
Simmer the sauce gently for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sugar dissolves and the tofu is hot throughout, reaching 74°C (165°F) in the center of a cube.

doneness_cues.visual: Small bubbles rise around the edges and the sauce lightly coats the spatula.

instructions.text: Slice the rested omelet into narrow ribbons on the cutting board while the sauce simmers.
Fold the drained noodles and garlic chives through the gently simmering sauce for 2–3 minutes with the spatula, until the noodles are tender and evenly coated.

doneness_cues.visual: The noodles are glossy, with a little loose sauce remaining.
doneness_cues.tactile: A sampled noodle is tender without a hard center.

instructions.text: Divide the sauced noodles and tofu between two serving bowls and arrange the omelet ribbons on top. Serve immediately.

troubleshooting.symptom: The noodles clump together and the sauce looks dry.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The noodles absorbed the sauce during prolonged cooking or standing.
troubleshooting.prevention: Stop cooking as soon as the noodles become tender, leave a little loose sauce in the skillet and serve promptly.
troubleshooting.fix: Fold in warm water in 15 g additions over low heat until the strands loosen and become glossy.

troubleshooting.symptom: The noodles break into short pieces.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: They were soaked until fully soft or stirred vigorously.
troubleshooting.prevention: Drain while slightly firm and use gentle lifting and folding motions in the sauce.
troubleshooting.fix: Stop stirring and portion carefully; broken strands cannot be restored.

chef_notes: Thai tao jiew supplies the sauce's fermented, savory depth. Stir the jar before weighing so the beans and salty liquid are evenly distributed.
Single-strength tamarind puree gives rounded acidity; highly concentrated extracts can overwhelm the coconut milk at the same weight.
Fine rice noodles continue absorbing liquid after cooking, so finish with a little more sauce than you want on the plate.

Cook the omelet to 71°C (160°F) and reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F), following [FoodSafety.gov minimum-temperature guidance](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures).
data.cultural_context: Mee kati is a Thai rice-vermicelli dish with coconut milk, and versions vary in their sauce, toppings and presentation. Some versions serve the coconut sauce separately or use pink-colored noodles; tofu and omelet also appear in vegetarian preparations. [Thai Food Made Easy](https://thaifoodmadeeasy.com/mee-ka-ti/)
